methodology_note: Per standing instruction: segments were researched and sized independently for each bar sub-category (energy, fruit & nut, protein, cereal/granola) BEFORE any purchasing-channel or targeting decision was made, to avoid skewing the table toward Yak Bar's assumed plan (health food stores, outdoor retailers). Purchasing behaviour/location columns reflect what the research says about where these personas actually shop, not the channels in phase0_discovery.json. Primary/secondary/not-target selection is a deliberately separate, later step performed by the user from the master tables below.
data_caveats: Category-specific AUS consumer data is uneven in depth and availability. Energy bar and protein bar personas have the strongest sourcing (including some AUS-specific stats). Fruit & nut bar and cereal/granola bar personas rely more heavily on adjacent-category proxies (protein bar buyer splits, general FSANZ snacking data, global children's snack bar reports) because dedicated AUS fruit-bar/cereal-bar consumer studies were not found via lightweight search. All price ranges (AUD) are flagged as ESTIMATES from general AUS retail observation, not sourced data -- a direct attempt to fetch sourced AUD pricing (nutrithrive.com.au) returned HTTP 403 and could not be used.

energy_bar_customers.category_context: Energy & Nutrition bars are Yak Bar's primary segment (100% overlap weight in Phase 1 SAM).

personas.segment_size_est: Not separately sized in available sources; part of the structured-sport segment of energy bar buyers.
personas.growth_rate_est: Tracks energy & nutrition bar CAGR per Phase 1 SAM (~8.9% blended AUS).
personas.profile_summary: Train and race at high intensity; need rapid, easily digestible fuel during effort. Prefer low-fibre (<=2g), high-carb bars (~40g carbs) for fast absorption -- the body can process only ~60g carbs/hour during activity. Ultra-distance events tolerate small protein additions (~5g) for muscle support.
personas.purchase_frequency: Very high during racing/training blocks (multiple bars per long session); otherwise occasional.
personas.purchasing_behaviour_location: Specialist run/triathlon stores, online (Maurten, SiS, and similar performance brands), sports nutrition retailers.
personas.needs: Fast carb absorption, low fibre/fat (avoid GI distress during exertion), proven race-day reliability.
personas.pain_points: High-fibre/fat 'natural' bars can cause stomach distress mid-race; flavour fatigue on long events.

personas.segment_size_est: Not separately sized; largest qualitative group in hiking-gear consumer content.
personas.growth_rate_est: Tracks energy & nutrition bar CAGR per Phase 1 SAM (~8.9% blended AUS).
personas.profile_summary: People who spend hours to days outdoors at a moderate, steady effort and eat multiple bars across a trip to keep going. Unlike racing athletes, they need sustained, balanced energy -- a mix of carbs, fats, and protein rather than a fast-carb hit or a high-protein bar -- and they value real-food taste, portability, and a bar that survives being packed.
personas.purchase_frequency: Trip-based (multiple bars per trip); several times/month for regular hikers.
personas.purchasing_behaviour_location: Outdoor/camping retailers, health food stores, online, before/during trips.
personas.needs: Sustained energy over hours, satiety, portability/durability (heat, packing), real-food taste.
personas.pain_points: Many 'energy' bars are sugar-spike/short-duration, not built for multi-hour sustained effort; bars melting/crumbling in packs.
personas.emotional_drivers: Adventure, self-reliance, enjoyment of the outdoors (lower performance-pressure than racing athletes).

personas.needs: Convenient pre/post-workout snack, reasonable nutrition, good taste.
personas.pain_points: Overlap/confusion with protein bar category; many bars feel either too 'sporty' or too indulgent.

energy_bar_customers.strategic_finding: Yak Bar's actual formulation (date/oat-based, higher fibre, balanced fat/carb/protein) maps more closely to the Outdoor Enthusiast need (sustained, balanced energy) than the Endurance Athlete need (low-fibre, fast-carb, GI-safe during high intensity). The higher-fibre, whole-food ingredients that support the 'natural' positioning are flagged in endurance-nutrition literature as a GI risk during high-intensity racing. This is reported as an honest finding, not adjusted to favour the product.

fruit_bar_customers.category_context: Fruit & Nut/Seed bars receive a 30% overlap weight in Phase 1 SAM (Yak Bar is ~20% date-based).
fruit_bar_customers.data_quality_note: Dedicated AUS fruit-and-nut snack bar consumer data is sparse; this table leans on adjacent-category proxies (protein bar buyer segments, FSANZ general snacking attitudes, global children's snack bar data, US organic-claims share). Frozen fruit bars (ice/dairy confection, USD 4.04bn to USD 6.93bn by 2032, 6.2% CAGR) were explicitly excluded as a different product category.

personas.pain_points: Confused by 'healthy halo' marketing vs actual sugar/additive content.

cereal_granola_bar_customers.strategic_finding: The cereal/granola buyer is largely price-driven, family/convenience-led, and mainstream -- a poor fit for a $3.50+ premium natural bar, consistent with Phase 1 weighting cereal at only 10% of the SAM overlap. The valuable overlap is the narrow 'health-conscious, lower-sugar, whole-grain' sliver, not the lunchbox volume core.
